en: Prosperity!
Oṃ, salutations to Gaṇeśa. The Goddess said:
To Śaṅkara, who was seated in Kāmarūpa, the beloved of Śaṅkara—
The goddess Yogamāyā, who is identical with the universe, questioned him with great reverence.
O Three-eyed Mahādeva, Lord and Master of all!
O God, O Lord, that worship of the Śiva-liṅga which was previously indicated by you— [please explain it].
O God, you are always meditated upon in my heart as being like my very life-breath;
now, O Supreme Lord, please cause me to recite [the mantra] correctly through your grace.
O Lord, having reflected upon the reality of the worship of the Śiva-liṅga, please explain it along with its primary and secondary limbs, as well as whatever secrets exist therein.
O Lord, gods, gandharvas, humans, asuras, and rakshasas—
all of them attain perfection through the worship of Shiva’s linga.
"O Lord Maheśvara, you have indeed previously indicated this, as have the other gods;
O Īśāna, tell me everything, if I am dear to you."
Īśvara said:
Listen, O mature daughter of the mountain, Menakā, delight of the mountains!
O Maheśānī, my ever-beloved, I shall here proclaim this knowledge.
O Supreme Goddess, when [the mantra] at the end of the feet is thus damaged,
O Great Goddess, I have given this [mantra] to the one who effects maintenance and withdrawal.
O Supreme Goddess, it is by the power of this knowledge that Viṣṇu becomes the sustainer and Brahmā becomes the creator of the universe.
O fair-faced one, O Goddess of gods, O ever-beautiful Yoginī, by the power of this knowledge I have conquered death; thus, O lady, I am Mṛtyuñjaya (the Conqueror of Death).
O Goddess of gods, among all forms of worship, the worship of the Liṅga is the supreme state.
O Goddess, he who performs any other form of worship without first worshipping the Liṅga [attains nothing].
That worship of his becomes distorted, and in the end he shall attain hell;
therefore, O Maheśānī, one should first worship the Liṅga.
O beloved, that kingdom which is constantly devoid of the worship of the Liṅga,
I consider that kingdom to be fallen, remembered as being equal to the ground of a funeral pyre.
O Goddess of the gods, even a knower of Brahman, if he does not worship the Liṅga, O Supreme Goddess,
shall at that very moment become an outcaste.
O Supreme Goddess, O beloved one dear to the best of gods, even a Śūdra should always worship the Śivaliṅga; indeed, all four castes beginning with the Brāhmaṇas [should do so].
O fair-limbed Pārvatī, know that house which is always devoid of the worship of Śiva to be equal to a pit of excrement.
O passionate goddess, in the house of one who performs worship other than that of Śiva, O Goddess, food becomes excrement and milk becomes urine.
For him, everything—even his worship and his food offerings—is equal to excrement;
his food is like excrement, and his milk is like urine, O fair-faced one.
O Supreme Goddess, O lady of excellent countenance, whether it be one's beloved, or a lord, or even a master,
one should first always worship him with *bilva* leaves.
Thereafter, O Great Goddess, one should pray to and worship another Śiva;
otherwise, O Beloved, everything [performed] without the worship of Śiva is like urine.
O beloved, whatever fragrant offerings, incense, and lamps have been prepared,
as well as water for the feet, the respectful offering, water for sipping, clarified butter, honey, and sugar;
Curd and milk, O Maheśānī; various beautiful flowers;
all kinds of fruits, O Bhadrā, as well as mangoes and grapes.
O beloved, let all things be praised as being equal to excrement;
therefore, among all forms of worship, the worship of the Liṅga comes first.
O fair-faced one, O Supreme Goddess, in all the Vedas, Tantras, and Purāṇas,
the worship of the Liṅga is proclaimed as the foremost.
O Goddess, without the worship of Śiva there is never any true worship;
whether in heaven, on earth, or in the netherworld, the worship of Śiva is the most supreme.
O Goddess, for those dwelling within the cosmic egg, the worship of Śiva is eternal wealth;
O Goddess, he who performs the worship of another deity without first performing the worship of Śiva [is lost].
O beloved, that very person, if deprived of the tongue, is born as a crocodile;
O Maheśānī, the worship of Śiva is praised above all dharmas.
Whatever merit exists among all dharmas and whatever wealth exists among all gifts—
that wealth one fully attains through the performance of worship of Śiva and other such acts.
Therefore, O beloved, with every effort one should always perform the worship of Śiva,
having fashioned an earthen liṅga of Rudra in his form as the Destroyer.
Having fashioned a linga according to the rules for Mahādeva— the eternally blissful one, whose banner is the bull— one should worship Śiva according to the prescribed rites.
O Goddess, by performing the secret rite according to the rules, one shall attain liberation;
one should worship with various flowers and most enchanting perfumes.
Then, with flowers of many varieties and fruits of many kinds.
[Thus ends the first chapter in the Liṅgārcanatantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 1 ||
The Goddess said: "O Lord, Śiva is remembered as being devoid of sense organs and having the nature of emptiness.
Since there is no cause for Śiva, how then can there be his worship?"
Īśvara said:
"Well asked, O Maheśānī! Listen, O Pārvatī, I shall speak;
O Maheśānī, O beautiful lady, there is never a time when the worship of the *preta* is absent."
O Supreme Goddess, the power of Rudra is known as Raudrī-śakti,
and the power of Viṣṇu is likewise proclaimed as Jyeṣṭhā-vaiṣṇavī-śakti.
O Kāminī, just as Vāmā is the power (śakti) of Brahmā,
so too, O Supreme Goddess, Raudrī is known to be the power of Rudra.
For Rudra, O Supreme Goddess, accompanied by Mahākuṇḍalinī,
abides eternally, O Goddess, within Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.
Enveloping Śiva, who dwells eternally, with three and a half coils, O Maheśānī; without Śakti, his state is certainly that of a preta.
By the mere conjunction with Śakti, Maheśvara is the agent and the destroyer;
for this very reason, O Maheśānī, one should worship the Śivaliṅga.
O Great Goddess, if the union of Śiva and Śakti occurs even once,
at that very moment arises the supreme knowledge esteemed in all the Vedas.
O fair-faced one, in all the Vedas, Tantras, and Purāṇas,
the supreme knowledge of Śiva and Śakti is proclaimed at one time.
Therefore, O Great Goddess, one should worship Śiva constantly;
O Supreme Goddess, the four castes beginning with the Brāhmaṇas should perform this worship.
Having worshipped with supreme devotion, the worshipper attains liberation;
O Maheśānī, O beloved, in whose house the worship of Śiva is performed constantly.
O Maheśānī, O Pārvatī, know that Kāśīpura is his home;
by worshipping the Śivaliṅga there, one obtains the fruit of all worship.
The Goddess said: O Mahādeva, the Śivaliṅga is endowed with supreme knowledge;
it is Brahman itself, O Mahādeva. Out of compassion, O Lord, please explain this.
"O God, the worship of the Śiva-liṅga has been directly taught; of this there is no doubt. The Lord said:
"Listen, O Goddess, I shall speak because of your devotion, O fair-faced one."
O Supreme Goddess, one should worship all those who dwell within the entire universe.
Having gone to the city of Mṛtyuñjaya, Brahmā and the other inhabitants of the celestial realms,
as well as the gods and others, abide in that abode consisting of the power of Śiva.
Having seen everything as consisting of knowledge through sight and the other senses, O beloved,
the one born of space (the ether) has thus passed through a cycle of four yugas, O beloved.
At the end of that, the dissolution lasts for as long; this is proclaimed as the Night.
In this very manner, the dissolution of the etheric element (*nābhasa*) occurs through illumination.
O Parameśānī, O beloved, Brahmā and the others fell into the state of a preta;
then, at the end of a hundred years, O beloved, from the mouth of Rudra, Raudrī [arose].
O Supreme Goddess, when cultivated, it becomes like a mountain of fire;
O Great Goddess, water and other elements are reduced to ashes by it in an instant.
O Maheśānī, having seen this wonder, curiosity arises within me;
O Parameśānī, by taking up the ashes, one attains the supreme state.
O Goddess of the gods, having smeared my body with ashes resembling the Śrī-mantra,
O Maheśānī, daughter of the mountain, I remained absorbed in meditation for a mere moment.
When the world, including the gods, asuras, and humans, has become a heap of ashes,
O Supreme Goddess, O Sovereign Lady, contemplate this within your heart.
O Supreme Goddess, a hundred thousand years have passed for me in meditation;
O Great Goddess of pure smiles, when I was in a state of meditative absorption.
At that very moment, O Supreme Goddess, the beloved one, assuming the form of a bull,
appeared before me and spoke a few words to me.
He spoke with auspicious words to the lotus-eyed Sundara:
"O Mṛtyuñjaya, O mighty-armed one, listen quickly to my words."
O Lord, that which was seen in my heart—I am Śānti by nature;
I am Kāminī in the form of a bull, Dharma himself in person, without a doubt.
Having heard what I have previously said, O King, worship Śiva;
Mahādeva is eternally and always present in the form of power (śakti), and she is his beloved.
"O Mahādeva, your beautiful vehicle Nandin is celebrated in this world by the name Dharmarāja; thus am I sung of, O Maheśvara."
"O Mahādeva, people constantly call me an owl;
O Lord, I am the very embodiment of Śakti—of this there is no doubt."
The mass of power that is Mahādeva is entirely established in you;
therefore, O Mahādeva, the King of Dharma is of the nature of your power.
Having assumed the form of a bull, I, the Great Lord Ulmuka, beheld everything as consisting of ghosts; then, O Lord, my power manifested.
Therefore, O Great God, he is known by the name Nirañjana;
the letter *u* is the goddess Umā, and the letter *ū* is Kāminī, O Lord.
The goddess Earth recognized the syllable *na*, O ocean of virtues;
and Mahādeva [recognized] the syllable *ka*—those two always [proclaim] you as the Jina.
Therefore, O Mahādeva, you are known by the name Ullūka, the bearer of yoga;
for you are indeed the Lord of all yogas and the eternal destroyer of death.
All the gods along with the gandharvas, Hari, the trees, and so forth—
even all those dwelling within the divine trees— have fallen into the state of pretas.
O God, you are indeed the eternal tree, free from the state of being a hungry ghost;
O All-pervading Lord, infinite powers reside within you, the portion.
The final bindu of the letter *ya*—for you, O God, are indeed the stainless one (*nirañjana*).
That which is the seventh seed-syllable (*bīja*) of the letter *ya*, O God, rich in asceticism.
O Mahādeva, O All-pervading Lord, he alone is the mass of power and the possessor of creation;
yet when you, O Supreme Lord, move through various states, O Master, he becomes Bhṛgu.
At that very moment, O Supreme Lord, stability and creation will certainly come to be;
O God, O Supreme Lord, you indeed enter the seed of Bhṛgu.
O Supreme Lord, at that very moment,
dissolution certainly occurs through the grace of the state of Mṛtyuñjaya and by the power of Sadāśakti.
"Having mounted my back, worship the auspicious Pārthiva. The Lord said:
"O Pārvatī, having heard the words of Ulmuka, he mounted the bull."
O Supreme Goddess, O Beloved, listen now to that which has been performed with haste.
Understand that the worship of the earthen linga was performed by her when she ascended the bull while it stood within, taking the form of a spear amidst the firebrands.
O Goddess of pure smiles, having ascended directly onto the wooden chest, you fashioned for me a Śiva-liṅga within that inner space.

O Great Goddess, O Beloved, O Pure-Smiling One, [I shall explain] the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi), as well as breath control (prāṇāyāma), the internal placement (antaryāsa), and the external placement (bahirnyāsa) beginning with the Mātṛkās.
O Maheśānī, O Pārvatī, O Supreme Goddess, whatever numerous nyāsas beginning with Śrīkaṇṭha have been described by me, O Great Sovereign.
O Maheśānī, O Parameśvarī, that which was stated in the Pūrvatantre—
having performed all of it in its entirety and in many ways, O Supreme Goddess.
O Great Goddess, O Supreme Sovereign, a hundred thousand years have passed for me in the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi),
having beheld the Goddess composed of bliss within the lotus of my heart.
O Maheśānī, having seen the Goddess—the mass of power—within whom all that is moving and unmoving resides;
the Goddess who has entered within the Suṣumnā, the Supreme Sovereign stationed there.
O Śiva, at that time, the deities and the trees and other beings exist there in a form as subtle as the finest barley-grain or vermilion.
Having seen her within the inner self, O Supreme Goddess, O Pārvatī;
when a hundred thousand years had passed, O Goddess, upon the peak of Mount Uṃmuka, O Pārvatī.
O Pārvatī, having first worshipped Dharma, my vehicle, O Goddess—
a firebrand and a bull— he is celebrated by the name Nandin.
O God, she who is the beloved woman is indeed Dharma and the other virtues, O dear one;
O Great Goddess, how could I venture to sustain myself without Śakti?
O Goddess of pure smiles, infinite powers reside within me; O Supreme Sovereign, it is by virtue of my power that I am indeed able to sustain all things.
O Maheśānī, Śakti herself is Dharma, and Vṛṣa himself is Dharma as well;
O Parameśānī, having first quickly worshipped Dharma—
Then, O Supreme Goddess, having performed the worship of the earthen liṅga in due order,
one should thereafter always look upon the leaf.
The Goddess said:
O God of gods, Mahādeva, the cause of creation, preservation, and destruction,
tell me truly, O Śaṅkara, the method of worshiping Dharmarāja.
Īśvara said:
"O lady of beautiful limbs, you who are the very embodiment of Dharma, my seat must be worshipped first, just as the worship of Dharma is performed."
I shall declare it, O Great Goddess; listen with full attention.
O Beloved, all [the rites], including bathing and sipping water (ācamana), are to be performed as previously described in the Tantra.
O Goddess of gods, O fair-faced one, having performed everything by means of the sequence of power (śaktikrama),
O Goddess of gods, O Supreme Sovereign, that which was spoken [is accomplished] by means of the seed-syllable of Dharma.
Having performed it with great effort, O Goddess, preceded by the nyāsa of the Mātṛkās, according to the previously mentioned Tantra, O Supreme Sovereign, first of all.
Having performed the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi), one should indeed perform the ritual placement of the Mātṛkās (mātṛkānyāsa).
Then, having performed breath control (prāṇāyāma), one should perform the ritual preparation of the offering water (arghyasthāpana).
O Goddess, O lady of excellent hips, one should perform the offering of the most difficult-to-obtain *arghya* according to the previously mentioned tantra;
remaining there, one should perform the recitation (*japa*) while employing the *varma* mantra.
Having performed everything as before, O Supreme Goddess, one should meditate upon the Supreme Sovereign, who possesses the form of Dharma, within the lotus of the heart as the beloved woman.
Listen, O lady of excellent limbs, to the description of meditation, which is manifestly of the nature of bliss,
possessing the radiance of ten million moons, and seated upon a white lion-throne.
Four-armed, long-armed, with lotus-like eyes and captivating,
he was adorned at his heart by a garland hanging down as far as his knees.
Adorned with white garments like camphor from the waves of the Gaṅgā,
endowed with a smile and side-long glances that enchant the three worlds.
O Goddess, O Supreme Sovereign, one should meditate upon the deity as a firebrand, the very embodiment of Dharma without cause; having thus contemplated with the mind within the heart-lotus.
Having worshipped [me], O Supreme Goddess, with mental offerings, O Sovereign Lady,
and having performed the mental recitation of the Dharma-mantra, O lady of pure smiles.
O Great Goddess, O passionate one, listen to the Dharma-mantra which I shall declare;
that which has not been spoken in any of the tantras, I shall now tell to you.
O Dear One, having first extracted the Praṇava and then the seed-syllable of the Elephant (Dantibīja),
join it with the syllable-seed and then apply the mudrā.
The word "dharma" ending in the dative case, followed by the wife of Vahni (svāhā);
this seven-syllabled vidyā bestows the fruits of the four aims of human life.
O Maheśānī, having recited the mantra one hundred thousand times and offered the sacrificial fee,
one should abandon [the practice] after mounting the bull named Ulūka, who is the very form of Dharma.
O Pārvatī, having worshipped the earthen liṅga according to the prescribed rite, [one attains the fruit].
[Thus ends the second chapter in the Liṅgārcanatantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī.]
Īśvara said:
O beloved, having taken ash from one's own body, one should fashion a liṅga;
O Maheśānī, in the absence of ash, one should make the liṅga out of clay.
But having seen this, O daughter of the mountain, I was filled with wonder;
"What shall I do? To whom shall I ask?"—thus I was overwhelmed by anxiety.
O Great Goddess, having carefully taken the ashes residing on the body,
the ash becomes manifest as moon-ointment through the touch of one's own limbs.
Oṃ viṃ, svāhā to Dharma.
Having taken in her hand, O Goddess of gods, that which is situated in the ashes and shines like sandalwood,
she should recite the Mātṛkā-mantra in both direct and reverse order.
Having softened the earthly [body] with the waters of the Gaṅgā and having fashioned it as the auspicious Śiva,
O Supreme Goddess, the Gaṅgā remains eternally within his matted locks.
Ganga is the mother of the three worlds, the eternal remover of sins;
she is the primordial source, the Mother of the Universe, manifest in the form of Shakti herself.
In this regard, O beloved, I shall now proclaim another teacher who is most difficult to find; for when Viṣṇu was present there for the sake of destroying the burden, he became that teacher.
O Great Goddess, hear the reason for his being known by the name Kṛṣṇa:
due to the curse of Brahmā, Kṛṣṇa resided within a Pippala tree, having taken refuge in Yama.
There, the hunter Durādharṣa, having bent his bow, struck Kṛṣṇa with an arrow aimed at the beauty of Kṛṣṇa’s feet, while uttering a curse he had prepared.
O Supreme Goddess, with an arrow fashioned of iron, he struck Kṛṣṇa’s foot in anger;
yet Kṛṣṇa’s hand remains ever [there].
O Goddess, O beloved, having been struck by the staff of the tree, he has gone to his own abode;
that blazing curse remains forever at the feet of Kṛṣṇa.
Then he indeed caused everything to burn away from Kṛṣṇa’s foot—
the tree's curse and his own unrighteousness— which had remained constantly in that foot.
O Supreme Goddess, it consumed the excellent body of Kṛṣṇa;
O lady of beautiful countenance, Viṣṇu quickly departed for the realm of Kṛṣṇa.
O fair-faced one, having previously learned everything regarding Kṛṣṇa’s curse,
he prostrated himself and spoke of the tree, O fair-faced one.
O Great Goddess, having heard the words of Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa Prajāpati spoke these sweet words to the all-powerful Viṣṇu.
Listen to my words, O Mahāviṣṇu: this is the medicine, the supreme medicine. The water of the Jāhnavī, which resides in my water-pot, is the medicine.
"O Lord of Gods, having washed your feet, become free from sin, O handsome one!
Gaṅgā, the mother of the three worlds, is the primordial power (Ādi-śakti) who pervades the universe."
O beloved, Hari, having first washed his feet with water from his water-pot (kamaṇḍalu),
then worshipped this Śiva, and thereafter [worshipped] the five-faced one (Pañcānana).
O Supreme Goddess, O Beloved, having cast off that sin through immersion,
O Sovereign Lady, that Hari quickly departed for Vaikuṇṭha.
Then, descending from his feet, she went forth as the one who flows through three paths;
on earth she is named Bhāgīrathī, and likewise in the underworld she is Bhogavatī.
In heaven, Mandrā Mahāmāyā, who manifests the glory of Viṣṇu,
went there, O Supreme Goddess, for the purpose of perceiving his meritorious form.
O Maheśānī, you are eternally established within my mass of matted hair;
O Maheśānī of beautiful countenance, you are earth, water, fire, air, and ether.
O Pārvatī, this reality is the great door, endowed with seven coverings;
all of it is encircled by wisdom during the dissolution within me.
O Goddess Pārvatī, know that the earth is adorned with its various manifestations;
O Supreme Sovereign, having gone to the waters at the edge of the matted locks, one should eat.
O Pārvatī, O Supreme Sovereign, know that which is heat to be fire;
know that wind which flows through the nose to be air, O Pārvatī.
O beloved, the region of the throat is the ether (ākāśa) of Śiva;
the Great Principle (mahattattva), the ego (ahaṅkāra), and primordial nature (prakṛti) are of the form of Śakti.
O Parameśānī, she is always established within the body of Śiva;
O Maheśānī, she is the supreme state that is the cause of the body.
Therefore, O Maheśānī, having softened the sandalwood paste and fashioned an earthen image,
O Goddess, it should be worshipped just like the vehicle.
Therefore listen, O lady of beautiful limbs, to this secret that is most difficult to obtain:
O Pārvatī, having turned toward the north, [perform it] over a firebrand.
O Supreme Goddess, O Sovereign Lady, listen, my beloved, as I declare everything that is accomplished by sitting in the lotus posture (padmāsana).
O Supreme Goddess, having fashioned a linga measuring one cubit,
it is a linga beautiful in all its limbs and beautiful in all its parts.
O Maheśānī, O Sureśvarī, she possesses a divine form and is Rudra himself in person;
O Parameśvarī, Nature (Prakṛti) is the Liṅga encircled by her joined palms.
O Goddess, from either one of these two arises the supreme Brahman, the highest state;
it is born at that very moment, O Goddess—of this there is no doubt.
And it has been said, O Pārvatī, that the earthly *liṅga* is distinguished by its clay:
white, red, yellow, and black, O Supreme Goddess.
White is prescribed for a Brāhmaṇa, red is desired for a Kṣatriya,
green for the Vaiśya caste, and black is proclaimed for a Śūdra.
And sandalwood, O Maheśānī, is praised in all births;
for sandalwood, O Maheśānī, is my ornament of prosperity.
Therefore, O blessed lady, sandalwood is indeed praised among all species;
O Goddess, this sandalwood unites the entire universe and serves as my ointment.
O Supreme Goddess, from burning comes the white form and ornament;
O Mistress of Gods, it is the seed of the universe, eternally composed of all powers.
O Maheśānī, O lotus-faced one, that ash is white in form;
that ash is the seed of the cosmic egg, which dwells eternally upon my body.
Whoever, having fashioned an image of sandalwood, should worship it,
thereby worships the entire universe, which bestows great liberation.
O Maheśānī, that brāhmaṇa who, having fashioned a white earthen liṅga, worships it, shall become a partaker of the three aims of life and noble lineage.
O lady of excellent hips, that Kṣatriya who, having fashioned a red earthen image,
constantly worships it, shall partake in the three aims of life and his lineage shall flourish.
O Goddess, O Maheśānī, he who, having fashioned a green earthen image, worships it, shall indeed become a Vaiśya and a partaker of the lineage of the three goals of life.
O Supreme Goddess, that Śūdra who, having fashioned a black earthen linga, worships it, shall become a partaker of the three aims of life (trivarga) and noble lineage.
O Supreme Goddess, O beautiful one, having gathered the Mṛtsūkta according to the distinction of its syllables through the Mātṛkā-mantras in both direct and reverse order, [one should proceed].
O Supreme Goddess, O Sovereign Lady, having recited the mantra ten times at the end in this manner,
O fair-faced one, one should indeed obtain the earth within those clods of soil.
O Goddess, who consists of all powers, O Embodiment, O Sovereign of the Thirty-three Gods! Having fashioned an earthen linga, I perform the worship of Śiva.
O Sovereign Goddess, adorned with various jewels, you have declared that Dharma, Artha, and Kāma are the gateways; O Goddess who bestows the fourfold aims of life!
O Supreme Goddess, how can happiness be known or spoken of without you? O Mistress of the Gods, neither wealth nor desire arises without you.
O Dear One, having recited the mantra "Oṃ Hrīṃ Mūrtike Duṣkṛti Hare Hrīṃ Oṃ," one should take up the clay image;
for the twelve-syllable mantra resides within my heart.
This is most secret, greatly meritorious, and bestows the four aims of human life.
O Supreme Goddess, if one should take the clay without knowing [the procedure],
his worship of the earthen Śiva shall be fruitless.
O lady of pure smiles, one should take it up with the mantra "oṃ harāya," or,
O beloved, the manifestation [should be performed] with the Mātṛkā mantras beginning with "oṃ maheśvarāya."
Having recited the Mātṛkā-mantra, O Śūlapāṇi,
and thereafter having recited "be well-established," one should then recite the Mātṛkā.
O Goddess, one should enjoin the vital breath (prāṇa) into the earthen Śiva-liṅga;
then, by means of the mantra for the installation of the vital breath, one should enjoin the prāṇa.
O Great Goddess, one should first proclaim the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi);
one should perform the purification of the elements and so forth according to the mantras previously mentioned.
Then, O lady of pure smiles, one should perform the nyāsa of the Mātṛkās with supreme effort; thereafter, having meditated upon Śiva, one should perform prāṇāyāma.
Having meditated upon Śiva Mahādeva, the cause of all the gods and others,
one should meditate upon him in sixteen ways, O Goddess of beautiful countenance, within the left channel.
O lovely-limbed one, O passionate woman, having filled [the body] with air through the path of meditation,
the wise practitioner, having performed the retention of the breath (vāyudhāraṇa), should perform exhalation (recaka).
O Goddess, O Supreme Sovereign, inhalation, retention, and exhalation—
this, O Goddess, is constantly remembered as prāṇāyāma of the vital breath.
The *prāṇa* is indeed proclaimed to be twelve *aṅgulas* in measure;
and the *prāṇa*, O Supreme Goddess, O lady of pure smiles, is self-knowledge.
O Maheśānī, that which is proclaimed as the vital breath (prāṇa) residing in all limbs exists in the heart, O beloved, in the form of the flame of a lamp.
O Maheśānī, the Supreme Brahman is like the flame of a lamp;
O Maheśānī, the inner self exists within the hearts of all.
The inner self, which is the Supreme Brahman, remains pervading the body;
O lady of excellent hips, the energy of these two is Śakti, whose form is Prakṛti.
O fair-faced one, O yoginī, at the time of breath control (prāṇāyāma), having seen a marvel,
listen to that which is the supreme secret as it has been taught.
[Thus ends the third chapter in the Liṅgārcanatantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 3 ||
The Lord said: O Supreme Goddess, as soon as that which was spoken regarding the Self being composed of Brahman was uttered, O Sovereign Lady,
a wondrous bliss was instantly perceived.
Having made it mind-made right there, O Maheśānī, O Pārvatī;
having become the mind within the nectar, O Maheśānī, O fair-faced one. (2)
O Maheśānī, O Parameśvarī, a hundred thousand years passed for me;
O Goddess, in the single moment of a breath-control (prāṇāyāma), a hundred thousand years of mine elapsed.
O Supreme Goddess, listen, O beloved, to that which has been seen and described;
there exists nothing higher than this within the scope of my perception. (4)
O Supreme Goddess, there is a couch of wondrous and marvelous form;
upon it is a bed resembling foam, adorned with various garments. (5)
O Supreme Goddess, that bed is Sadāśiva, the Great Cloth;
upon it, O Great Goddess, lies Tripurasundarī asleep.

One should meditate upon the beloved woman who has the appearance of vermilion mixed with barley and barley-gruel, who possesses four arms and three eyes, and who holds the five arrows and the bow. || 7 ||
Having beheld the Supreme Goddess, who holds the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness,
who is composed of bliss and ever-fickle, a hundred thousand years passed for me.
And when, O Supreme Goddess, she came within the range of my vision,
at that very moment she suddenly assumed a subtle form.
O Maheśānī, O beautiful one, at that very moment my meditation was broken;
right there I beheld the cosmic egg and the celestial dwellers beginning with Brahmā.
O Maheśānī, O beloved, without Śakti there is nothing whatsoever in me;
for Śakti is the form of Brahman, a mass of power, O fair-faced one. (11)
O Maheśānī, without Śakti nothing at all comes within my range;
thus indeed, O Goddess, is the unsurpassed Prāṇāyāma performed in due order.
O Goddess, when breath control (prāṇāyāma) has been performed, one should perform the supreme Mātṛkā-nyāsa;
O Maheśānī, having performed the nyāsa, [one should meditate upon] the Mātṛkā who deludes the universe. 13.
Henceforth, O lady of excellent hips, one should perform the Śrīkaṇṭha-nyāsa;
by the mere performance of the Śrīkaṇṭha-nyāsa, O lotus-faced one, I am Śiva. (14)

O Parameśānī, Śrīkaṇṭha is worshipped even throughout the three worlds; O Kāminī, everything is as previously described in the Tantra, with the specific addition that he is worthy of the arghya offering.
O Maheśānī, O Supreme Goddess, one should perform everything with diligence;
O lotus-eyed Maheśānī, one should meditate upon Śiva in the lotus of the heart.
O Supreme Goddess, within the heart-lotus resides the captivating knowledge of Brahman;
it is here that the station of the individual soul is said to be, the heart being the supreme abode. (17)
The heart-lotus has twelve petals and possesses the brilliance of a thousand suns;
in its center, O beloved, one should meditate upon the god Śiva, the conqueror of death.
Resembling pure crystal, with five faces and great luster,
O Goddess of gods, his arms reach down to his knees, and his eyes have the hue of red lotuses.
Wearing a crown and earrings, beautifully adorned with a lion’s mane, he was ever endowed with a smile and resplendent with a row of teeth. (20)
His chest was adorned with rudrākṣa beads, his head was graced with matted locks,
he was clothed in a tiger skin, and he shone with ten arms.
Having thus meditated upon Mahādeva, who is eternally the conqueror of death, O beloved—
upon Mahādeva who is endowed with Śakti, the omniscient one, and the deluder of all— 22.
Having performed contemplation on the Omniscient One, one should thereafter contemplate a single limb;
and by relinquishing even that single limb, meditative absorption (samādhi) is then born.
O Goddess of gods, listen to that most beautiful knowledge regarding the splendor which arises during the time of meditative absorption. 24.
O beloved Parameśānī, that splendor which arises from the abandonment of even omniscience is indeed Śiva, the conqueror of death. 25.
Know, O Pārvatī, that the primordial nature (prakṛti) has the form of a lamp-flame;
within that light, O Goddess of the Gods, the wondrous Self (adbhutātmā) is eternally situated. (26)
O Maheśānī, O Parameśvarī, the wondrous-souled one, having bound the male bee (the individual soul) and the female bee (the intellect) within the heart-lotus, is devoid of cause and effect.
O Maheśānī, established in yoga for a hundred thousand years, my elephant was mine;
at that time, O Goddess, O beloved, it became a female bee.
O Maheśānī, O beloved, having seen that city of Ājñā, the bee immediately flew toward it with great restlessness, O lotus-faced one. (29)
Know, O Pārvatī, that both the effect and the cause are indeed Prakṛti;
having thus become intent on meditation, hear, O beloved, what was accomplished.
And the bee, O Maheśānī, together with the female bee, O beautiful one, was recognized by each other through the noose of knowledge, O lady of pure smiles. (31)
O Supreme Goddess, having become established upon the six lotuses and always joined with the drinking of honey,
the female bee is the direct bestower of liberation.
O Maheśānī, wherever the beautiful Bhramarī went, there the bee also went quickly, O Maheśānī. (33)
O Goddess, when Bhramarī had departed, a breach in my yoga occurred;
yet while I remained established in yoga, O lady of beautiful limbs, the most wonderful City of Six (Ṣaṭpura) appeared.
O Supreme Mistress of the Six Cities, O Beloved, you are eternally composed of light;
[you reside in] that divine city, full of light and filled with the supreme nectar.
"O auspicious one, having seen the lotus grove, my female bee never returns; O Queen of the Gods, O beloved, she does not depart from the forest. (36)
The Śrī Devī said:
"O Supreme Lord, how is it that a bee is born there?
O Maheśāna, how did the noose of knowledge enter the space of consciousness? (37)
Īśvara said: O Goddess, because the female bee is the follower of the bird,
for that very reason, O Maheśānī, these limbs of mine constitute Yoga.
For this very reason, O Great Goddess, one should perform the external worship;
facing the Destroyer (Bhairava), O Pārvatī, [one should do so] upon a firebrand.
Having sat down, O Maheśānī, just as one whose vehicle has been worshipped, I shall speak; listen, O lady of excellent complexion, as I declare all of that. (40)
Having thus performed the internal worship, one should perform the external worship as previously described.
[Thus ends the fourth chapter in the Liṅgārcanatantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 4 ||
The Lord said: O Supreme Goddess, having first performed everything exactly as previously described in the Tantra with great effort, one should then practice external meditation.
O Goddess of the gods, having performed the previously mentioned meditation, one should cast a flower [upon] the pavilion,
which is indeed red in color and endowed with four doors.
O Supreme Goddess, having presented one who is well-dressed, beautiful, and charming upon the back of Nandin, O Great Sovereign, and having placed him upon sandalwood paste;
It is quadrangular with four doors, endowed with supreme knowledge;
listen, O beloved, regarding the southern altar of the self and the eastern altar.
O Goddess, that altar which is in the eastern direction is sung of as the inner self (antarātman);
and that altar which is in the north, O Goddess, is sung of as the supreme self (paramātman).
O Goddess, that altar which is in the west is proclaimed to be the essence of knowledge;
in its four-cornered square are the eight supernatural powers, beginning with *aṇimā*.
O Goddess, these are ever-present; there is no need for deliberation here.
Aṇimā is to be known on the eastern altar, and Mahimā in the south-eastern corner.

O Pārvatī, pervasion (vyāpti) is indeed in the south-west; O Goddess, the power of irresistible will (prākāmya) is in the south-east; greatness (mahimā) is in the west, O Goddess, and mastery (īśitā) is in the north-west corner.

O Goddess of gods, Vaśitā is in the upper [direction], and Kāmasundarī is in the northeast (aiśāna). O Supreme Sovereign, having fashioned a beautiful *bindu* in the center of that, [one should worship].
In the center of that, O Supreme Goddess, O fair-faced one, having written the seed-syllable of Kāma— the seed-syllable consisting of all power, O beloved Queen of the Gods.
O Dear One, having encircled the square and drawn two coils,
O Supreme Goddess, one should draw the world-enchanting Kuṇḍalī.
O Great Goddess, within a square one should write a square [mandala] and the Praṇava;
then, O Supreme Goddess, one should write the eight seed-syllables in sequence.
O Supreme Goddess, listen as I shall explain that seed-syllable in due order: O Beloved, having written the syllable Abhaya joined above with the Bindu, O Goddess.
O Maheśānī, having first placed the seed-syllable of Earth (la) conjoined with a bindu above it,
then follow the seed-syllable of Śakti (ha), O beloved, likewise conjoined with a bindu above it.
Again, O Maheśānī, having always written the Śakti as before,
one should form the fifth vowel (u), O Maheśānī, joined with a Bindu above.
O Supreme Goddess, having joined the left eye with the Bindu with supreme effort,
and having joined it with the seed-syllable of Vala, one should write it down.
O Maheśānī, it possesses eight seed-syllables and bestows the eight sovereign powers;
O beloved Mahākuṇḍalinī, it envelops everything, O Maheśānī.
O lady of tremulous glances, having inscribed the mantra whose form is the universe at the outer corner of the door, O lady of pure smiles, [draw] an eight-petaled lotus.
Having carefully and with great effort drawn this beautiful and most enchanting form,
O lady of excellent hips, it remains forever situated within my heart.
O daughter of the mountain, it is by the power of this mantra that I have attained perfection;
O Great Goddess, this mantra is very difficult for even gods and asuras to obtain.
Henceforth, O Maheśānī, O Pārvatī, listen to the description of the Nirmāṇa [form];
it should be made of sandalwood, O Maheśvarī, measuring exactly one cubit.
Having fashioned a linga according to the prescribed rites out of sandalwood,
measuring exactly one cubit in length, O Goddess worshipped by the gods!
O Dear One, having established [the deity] in the center of the mantra above the seed-syllable of desire (kāmabīja),
and having performed worship and meditation, one should cast [the oblation] upon it.
O Maheśānī, the bilva leaf consists of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva;
O Goddess, its three leaves represent the three qualities (guṇas) and bestow all things at all times.
Then, O Supreme Goddess, having formed a mental resolve,
he remained as Mahādeva within the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa) just as before.
"Let it be so, O Brahmāṇḍa," and even that very resolve—O Goddess of gods, O Supreme Sovereign, that [resolve] is to be kept secret from me; thus she bowed.
O Supreme Goddess, O beloved, at that time neither my mother nor my father exists for me; indeed, O Great Sovereign, O dear one, nothing whatsoever belongs to me.
O Goddess of pure smiles, at that time there was no lunar day (vāra), no lunar date (tithi), no degree (kāṣṭhā),
and no minute fraction (kalā), O Goddess of beautiful countenance.
Neither by day, O Supreme Goddess, nor by night, O Supreme Sovereign;
for this very reason, O Great Mistress, it is known as the mental resolve (saṃkalpa).
O Beloved, if it enters the mind, then what need is there for the gross?
O Goddess, mental resolve bestows the fourfold aims of life.
O Supreme Goddess, gross resolve is said to be futile;
O Goddess, whatever a wise person has done without resolve is likewise so.
O Supreme Goddess, all that which has been spoken is supreme and mental;
O Supreme Goddess, [so too is] that which has been spoken by the sage of limited intellect.
O Pārvatī, O Supreme Sovereign, all that becomes useless;
having thus formed this resolve, one should perform the *jīvanyāsa*.
O Great Goddess, listen attentively to the jīvananyāsa:
prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, and vyāna.
O Goddess, these five vital breaths reside within my heart;
O Maheśānī, Prāṇa is in the heart, while Apāna is in the anus, O Dear One.
The *samāna* wind is at the region of the navel, while the *udāna* is from the region of the throat;
the *vyāna*, O Supreme Goddess, remains pervading the entire body.
O Maheśānī, one should practice these winds with the *praṇava*;
O Maheśānī, at each lotus, a mass of splendor is produced.
O beloved, having led that light into the left nostril within the *praṇava*,
O Goddess Pārvatī, let it rest for a hundred thousand times in the left nostril.
Then, O Supreme Goddess, having cast that vital energy, which resembles the hibiscus flower,
into the Śiva-linga, O lotus-faced one, that energy—
Having done this, O Great Goddess, hear from me the mantra of Vāyu; O lady of excellent limbs, listen attentively to these five mantras.
O Goddess of gods, one should utter "oṃ prāṇāya" and at the end recite "svāhā";
O you who are worshipped by the gods, [the mantra] ends with "oṃ apānāya svāhā."
"Oṃ samānāya svāhā," ending with *svāhā*, O Goddess praised by the gods;
"oṃ udānāya svāhā," ending with *svāhā*, O fish-eyed one.

"Oṃ vyānāya svāhā"— having thus recited these five mantras ending with *svāhā* at all times, and having indeed deposited the vital breath (*prāṇa*) upon Śiva while holding Śiva constantly with the *jñānamudrā*, O Maheśānī.
O Goddess of gods, O Pārvatī, listen to the special procedure for the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (invocation of the vital breaths).

Having uttered: *oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ kṣaṃ sauṃ namaḥ śivāya*, [one says]: "Whatever has been performed by me, may the vital breaths (*prāṇāḥ*) of this wielder of the trident (*śūlapāṇiḥ*) be here, the vital breaths. [Then] the previous mantra.
Having first recited "of this wielder of the trident (śūlapāṇeḥ)," then reciting all the sense organs again, one should say:
"Of this wielder of the trident, speech, mind, eye, ear, breath, and vital forces—having come here, may they remain for a long time, svāhā! Thus it is said.
Then again, O Maheśānī, having recited the six-syllable mantra "Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya" seven times, O Dear One;
O Supreme Goddess, having placed at the end the *liṅga* fashioned by Śrīkaṇṭha,
thereafter, O Great Goddess of beautiful countenance, one should offer water for the feet (*pādya*).
O Goddess of gods, O lady of excellent complexion, having offered the *arghya* and *ācamanīya* to the auspicious *liṅga*, I performed the meditation previously described.
O Goddess, beloved of the sweet-voiced cuckoo, O lady of pure smiles,
having performed meditation ending with the heart-mantra, [offer] a flower, O lady of pure smiles.
O Goddess of gods, having placed a beautiful bilva leaf upon the liṅga,
one should then, O Supreme Sovereign, invoke the Supreme Lord.
O Goddess of the Universe, O beautiful one, having performed everything as previously described in the Tantra, I have offered the threefold libation (tarpaṇa) through the non-duality of the Self.
Then, O Supreme Goddess, having recited the prayer-mantra:
"Come, O Lord of the gods of gods; remain firmly established here in this linga."
O Mahādeva, having stood forth, accept this worship; salutations be unto you!
By your grace, O Lord of Gods, I shall fashion the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa).
Then, O Goddess, having worshipped the Lord of the gods of gods— the Liṅga born of Śrīkaṇṭha— with each of the sixteen services individually, [one should proceed].
Then, O Goddess, having offered a salutation with joined palms out of devotion to Śiva,
one should offer everything, O Maheśānī, into the Liṅga born of Śrīkaṇṭha.
At that time, O Goddess, with valorous strides to the left, O lady of beautiful limbs, I shall speak to you what was said to me; listen, my beloved.
[Thus ends the fifth chapter in the Liṅgārcanatantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 5 ||
Īśvara said: "O Mṛtyuñjaya, O mighty-armed Lord,
at first I was unable, O Mahādeva, to support the liṅga at any time."
O Mahādeva, O Lord of Gods, how can I support a second Śiva standing upon my back in the intermediate space, O Lord?
Forgive me, O Lord of the gods; have mercy upon me, O Master!
Salutations to you, O Lord of the gods, the Supreme Lord, the Ancient One.
"Salutations to you, O Lord of the worlds! Victory over Death, homage be unto you!
Having heard the words of Ulmuka, [the Lord said], "O beloved, what shall I do?"
O Goddess of gods, O Pārvatī, I was filled with anxiety at that very moment;
O Great Goddess, O Pārvatī, I became absorbed in meditation at that very moment.
Having meditated upon the Goddess within the heart— she who consists of lightning,
who resides within the heart-lotus, the beautiful one, and whose form is subtle.
"O Maheśānī, O fair-faced one, having seen this form which is directly composed of mantra, divine, sixteen-fold, and the bestower of liberation— truly a marvel!"
O lady of pure smiles, [I have attained] that supreme and subtle knowledge which was propitiated by me—
the knowledge situated within the *suṣumnā*, which bestows dharma, desire, wealth, and liberation.
Supreme, consisting of Brahman, eternal, having the nature of the Śabdabrahman,
with a form like vermilion and resembling barley-alkali or lac-dye.
Having prostrated before the Supreme Goddess, who resembles the rising sun,
and having recited the Śrīvidyā, the Supreme Goddess, O Parameśānī;
O Goddess, O Supreme Sovereign, having mentally recited [the mantra] ten times,
that Goddess resides within the inner self, just as I have described to you, O Pārvatī.
Listen now to that secret; I shall tell you the essence of knowledge.
Do not fear, do not fear, O Mahādeva, O Mṛtyuñjaya, O Sadāśiva!
O Supreme Lord, O Treasure of Austerity, there is nothing whatsoever apart from me;
this entire universe, O Mahādeva, is comprised of seven coverings.
O Mahādeva, all this universe exists within me;
O Lord Mahādeva, without Śakti, nothing whatsoever exists.
O Mahādeva, without Śakti, the universe is always like a corpse;
O Lord of Gods, when the dissolution occurs, everything is withdrawn into me.
When this had been spoken, O lady of beautiful limbs, she went to Śaktipura like a flash of lightning.
Īśvara said:
"O Supreme Goddess, that which was mentioned by you, O Parameśvarī, is indeed that lightning."
Listen, O Great Goddess, to this secret; I shall speak to you the essence of knowledge.
O Mṛtyuñjaya, O mighty-armed one, delusion arises;
for this worship, O Lord Sadāśiva, is born of delusion.
O Lord of excellent vows, Śrīvidyā is always most worthy of worship for you;
therefore, O Supreme Lord, how could you, O Master, abandon your beloved Vidyā?
O Goddess, having first recited the desired mantra, one should worship [the deity];
for this alone, O Lord, is superior to the feeble firebrand.
"Now remember me, O Lord of Gods, O Sadāśiva, conqueror of death!
Having heard her words, he then bowed down to her, whose form is liberation.
Then, having consoled Ulmuka, he said: "Listen, my dear;
O Viśva, you are indeed Ulmuka, and I shall speak an excellent boon."
But in the Kali age, O illustrious Lord of true valor, your manifestation will take place in Bhāratavarṣa as Ulmuka.
O illustrious one, you are the beloved woman; you are Dharma, assuming a white form. Yet in the Kali age, during your worship, whoever has even a single thought of another in their mind—
O Supreme Goddess, whether they be Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, or those of Śūdra birth,
their disease arises at that very moment.
O Great Goddess, the breaking of my yoga occurs at that very moment;
for if one does not recite the desired mantra, an obstacle arises from that.
He who does not know that everything is composed of the power of the universe (jagat-śakti) is a denizen of hell;
O Maheśānī, O Sundarī, having brought about the disruption of yoga, whatever was done [is lost].
Listen to all that regarding the sacrifice of the king, O lovely-limbed one, my dear;
for, O woman of excellent complexion, you must contemplate the lotus-face of Śiva.
Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, Aghora,
and thereafter Tatpuruṣa and Īśāna— these are proclaimed as the five faces.
Sadyojāta is indeed white, endowed with white splendor;
likewise, Vāmadeva is yellowish-white, gentle, and captivating to the mind.
The Aghora [face] is black in color and equal [in its nature], while the Bhīma [face] increases [fear];
the Tatpuruṣa deity is red, possessing a divine form that is captivating to the mind.
One should meditate on the first [form], Śyāmala, and likewise Īśāna, who is the essence of all gods and Śiva, in the west; and the second in the north.
One should meditate with devotion, intent on the deity Aghora in the south, Tatpuruṣa in the east, and likewise know Īśāna to be in the center.
O Maheśānī, O fair-faced one, I shall now declare the fivefold mantra;
O Goddess of gods, O Supreme Sovereign, by reciting which I am Mṛtyuñjaya (the Conqueror of Death).
Of all the vowels, the remaining long ones are accompanied by the bindu;
those excluding *ṛ* and *ḷ* are always joined with the half-moon and the *praṇava*.
O Great Goddess, it always has five faces and consists of the five elements:
earth, the seed-syllable of wind, water, and space itself.
Thus, O Maheśānī, one should meditate upon the five elements as the supreme state— the reality itself— according to the sequence of Sadyojāta, O Parameśvarī.
In sequence, those known as *sanmada*, *sanmoha*, *nāda*, and *gaurava*,
along with *prasāda* when it has become nourished (*puṣṭa*), are proclaimed as the five mantras.
The mantra that causes delight to Śambhu is called *sanmat*;
and having reached the complete fulfillment of the mind, it is proclaimed as *sanmoha*.
O Maheśānī, the Nāda-mantra is proclaimed as the means of attraction;
indeed, it is the most excellent and venerable mantra, bestowing dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa.
O Supreme Goddess, the temple is said to bestow prosperity;
one should worship each individual face with its respective mantra.
Having combined them into one, one should indeed worship with five;
this, O Maheśānī, is the reality, the very essence of the knowledge of Śiva.
For all beings, beginning with the immobile, the essence of knowledge is very difficult to attain;
through devotion to you, I have declared this essence of knowledge that is so hard to find.
[Thus ends the sixth chapter in the Liṅgārcanatantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Parvatī. || 6 ||
Furthermore, O Great Goddess, O beloved, listen to the essence of knowledge,
by the mere remembrance of which all calamities come to an end.
One should constantly meditate upon Mahādeva, whose splendor is like that of a mountain of silver,
who is endowed with a smile, whose face is gracious, and who has the orb of the moon as his ear-ornament.
The god with reddened eyes, five-faced and enchanting,
endowed with a mass of matted hair, and possessing three eyes in each face.
The god is seated upon a yoga-lotus, adorned with a garland of severed heads,
decorated with sacred ashes, and clothed in a tiger skin.
One should thus meditate upon the God, the eternal God of gods, who has four arms, a massive body, and always holds a rosary of beads.
Having reflected thus upon the Lord of all the lords of gods,
O fair-faced one, perform worship like that for the eight supernatural powers beginning with *aṇiman*.
Then, O fair-faced one, having worshipped them with their respective mantras using bilva leaves,
O Maheśānī, O lady of pure smiles, one should employ the dative case ending (caturthī) for the sake of attaining success.
O lady of pure smiles, first utter the Praṇava; then extract the seed-syllable again, ending it with the dative case;
then, having extracted the seed-syllable once more, follow that with the Praṇava at the end.
By this very procedure, O lady of pure smiles, one should worship the Eight Vidyās;
having worshipped the Eight Vidyās, O Great Goddess, you who are honored by the gods.
O Maheśānī, O beautiful one, having worshipped according to the rules with devotion in each corner and in the four directions, and having recited the mantra and offered praise, O lady of pure smiles!
O Great Goddess, having performed the worship of Śiva, who possesses eight forms,
listen, O Supreme Sovereign, O fair-faced one, to how it is done.
O Maheśānī, having worshipped the eightfold form (Aṣṭamūrti) at the doorway,
O Parameśānī, one becomes perfected by always worshipping according to the prescribed rite.
O Maheśānī, O beautiful one, listen to the names of the Eight-formed Lord;
having worshipped them with supreme devotion in the sequence beginning from the front.
Listen, O lady of beautiful limbs, to the ritual application that always resides within my heart:
*Oṃ, obeisance to Śarva, whose form is earth;
Oṃ, obeisance to Bhava, whose form is water.*
Oṃ, salutation to Rudra, whose form is fire.
Oṃ, salutation to Ugra, whose form is wind.
Oṃ, salutation to Bhīma, whose form is space.
Oṃ, salutation to Paśupati, the embodiment of the sacrificer.
Oṃ, salutation to Mahādeva, the embodiment of Soma.
Oṃ, salutation to Īśāna, the embodiment of the Sun.
Having performed the worship, O Maheśānī, according to this procedure, O beloved;
now, O Maheśānī, I shall tell you another [teaching], the essence of knowledge.
O Maheśānī, having worshipped Aṣṭaviṣṇu immediately thereafter,
O Parameśānī, one should worship Kuṇḍalī, who encircles the exterior.
O Great Goddess, I shall proclaim to you the names of the eightfold Viṣṇu:
Ugra, Viṣṇu, Mahāviṣṇu, Ananta, and Saṃpratāpana.
Nṛsiṃha, Bhīṣaṇa, Bhīma, and the one proclaimed as Mṛtyumṛtyu—
O Maheśānī, listen to how one should worship these forms of Viṣṇu.
O Goddess, having worshipped the imperishable Viṣṇu through the sequence beginning with *saṃ* and *mā*,
listen, O lady of beautiful limbs and lovely face, to that mantra which is the essence of knowledge.
"Oṃ, obeisance to the fierce Viṣṇu"—thus [one pays homage] to Mahāviṣṇu;
then, "Oṃ, obeisance to the infinite Viṣṇu"—thus [one pays homage] to Saṃpratāpana Viṣṇu.
Oṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu in the form of Nṛsiṃha; salutation to the terrifying Viṣṇu. Oṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu in the form of Bhīma. Oṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu, the death of Death.
O Great Goddess, O Supreme Sovereign, having performed this worship,
I have attained the knowledge of Viṣṇu, endowed with all powers.
Then, O lady of excellent hips, O lady of pure smiles, the imperishable Viṣṇu was worshipped with the sixteen services, while the mantra was being externally invoked.
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, she who is the mother of all mothers is herself honored;
for that which is declared in the ancient Tantras as the supreme Mātṛkā-mantra [is she].
O Great Goddess, by these mantras, the Mātṛkā— beginning with the letter 'a' and ending with the letter 'kṣa', the Mātṛkā whose form is Brahman— has been worshipped by me.
She is the mother of all, the Sovereign in the form of the Mother;
O Supreme Goddess, without her, even Speech would fall into insentience.

O Supreme Goddess, O Goddess worshipped by the gods, having worshipped that Goddess according to the rule and according to the prescribed rite as the witness in the form of a *kalā*, [one should proceed].
O Goddess, O beautiful one, for the sake of protecting herself and the universe,
O Supreme Sovereign, that woman is a Mātṛkā, O lady of pure smiles.
Therefore, O Daughter of the Mountain, one should worship the Goddess Mātṛkā at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end; otherwise, obstacles will arise.
Indeed, everything is exactly like the previously mentioned mantra, being the Mātṛkā-mantra itself;
having worshipped it according to the rule, one should thereafter worship Gaṇeśa.
Having worshipped with supreme devotion using perfumes, flowers, and other offerings, O beloved, thereafter,
O lady of excellent hips, one should worship Viṣṇu on the right.
O Supreme Goddess, having worshipped Gaurī Mahāmāyā on the left,
one should then worship Viṣṇu with "Oṃ Viṣṇave Namaḥ" on the right, and Gaurī with "Gaurye Namaḥ" on the left.
O Goddess, having worshipped the wonderful Liṅga according to this procedure,
one should satisfy Śiva three times with the various mantras beginning with *ĀM*.
Henceforth, O lady of excellent hips, O beloved, listen to how one should perform the recitation (japa),
which is the essence of knowledge, higher than the highest, O fair-limbed one.
Then, O Maheśānī, O lady of excellent complexion, having meditated upon the charming linga within the heart-lotus, one should mutter the fivefold mantra.
O lady of pure smiles, having recited the mantra from the letter 'a' to the letter 'kṣa'— which is proclaimed as being present— in both direct and reverse order, one should worship the liṅga.
O fair-faced one, O Great Goddess, [visualize] a subtle rosary within the Suṣumnā,
variegated and adorned with many diverse colors.
That which is situated within the Suṣumṇā is called the navel;
it consists of Śiva and Śakti, O lotus-faced one, and is eternal.
O lady of pure smiles, having taken up the rosary and performed a hundred thousand recitations,
she beheld wonderful bliss within the great thousand-petaled lotus.
Bliss is the form of Brahman; this is the embodied Prakṛti.
O beloved, O Great Preta Sadāśiva, the city of Śakti has been seen.
O Goddess, having made the garland one that is eternally bowed, it dissolves right there;
O Maheśānī of pure smiles, recite that syllable a hundred thousand times.
At that moment, O Goddess, the mind dissolves into Brahman;
having beheld the nectar-like Śakti in the city of Sadāśiva, O Goddess.
Or rather, O beloved, listen to that which has been described as the six-syllable mantra to be recited.
[Thus ends the seventh chapter in the Liṅgārcanatantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 7 ||
Īśvara said: [She who is] more subtle than the most subtle, supreme, resembling vermilion,
four-armed, three-eyed, and bearing the five arrows and the bow.
The Supreme Goddess is clothed in red garments, adorned with girdles of tinkling bells,
and graced by the resonant jingling of anklets and other ornaments.
The Goddess is adorned with conch shells, bracelets, armlets, bangles, and other ornaments; she possesses two breasts and is resplendent with a necklace of large pearls.
The Goddess who embodies all the gods, the auspicious Śivā who embodies all the gods,
whose lotus feet are touched by the crest-jewels upon the heads of Brahmā and Viṣṇu.
She holds the two mudrās, namely the Abhaya and the Varada,
and she has the Gaṅgā, Yamunā, and Śoṇa rivers situated within her eyes.
O Maheśānī, seeing her with smooth vermilion [tilaka] resembling the dawn-red of morning, bliss arises within me.
O Maheśānī, O beloved, I have forgotten the six-syllabled japa;
O Supreme Goddess, O lady of pure smiles, [forgive] that Śrīvidyā in my mouth.
O Supreme Goddess, Śrīvidyā always resides within my heart,
and likewise, the Kālikā-vidyā shines upon her throat.
Now follows the origin of the ten Mahāvidyās:
O Maheśānī, Bhuvaneśī is the Mahāvidyā on her right arms; O Dear One, Bhairavī belongs to her left arm.
O Supreme Goddess, Chinnamastā is in her heart;
likewise, Mātaṅgī and Vagalādevī are in her two feet.
O Maheśānī, Lakṣmī is in her navel, O lotus-faced one;
and on her crown, O Maheśānī, is Mahiṣamardinī herself.
O Supreme Goddess, O Beloved, the fifty goddesses of the Mātṛkā reside within the fifty locations and junctions, abiding by means of their own essential forms and so forth.
O Great Goddess, having beheld within her mouth the supreme syllable Vidyā— the goddess who consists of all the Āgamas, who is beautiful, and whose form is liberation—
O Supreme Goddess, having beheld that Vidyā within the lotuses of their hearts,
they proclaimed the supreme knowledge, the most excellent Śrīvidyā mantra.
O Parameśānī, having performed one hundred thousand recitations arising from the mind,
O Goddess, by uniting the self with the mind in the highest manner.
Having chanted thus, O Maheśānī, one hundred thousand years passed for me;
the arrival of the *svāhā* [mantra], O Maheśānī, consists of two syllables arising from the *ajapā*.
O Maheśānī, her own self resides upon her head;
beyond that, O Varārohā, O beloved, she has reached the state of the Bhramarī.
O Goddess, daughter of the Naga, the passionate female bee quickly went with the male bee to the *mūlādhāra* to drink the honey.
Having bound the *bhramarī* [mudrā], O Goddess of pure smiles, with the face turned upward,
one reaches the delightful city of Sadāśiva, where she who is liberation itself resides.
O Great Goddess, by reciting the Śrīvidyā, the Supreme Sovereign, one hundred thousand times mentally,
my Yoga shall be shattered at that very moment.

O Supreme Goddess, O lady of pure smiles, the bee [of consciousness], having formed the Bhramarī mudrā with hands displaying the *siddhi* gesture, goes from city to city throughout the cycles of creation and the rest.
But having bound the bee, O Goddess, which is the stainless form of Brahman,
[one attains it], O Supreme Mistress of all, including creation and the rest, O lady of pure smiles.
O Goddess, the male bee is undoubtedly the cause of liberation and other [spiritual goals];
but, O Great Goddess, the female bee is the cause of the male bee.
O Goddess, O lotus-faced one, the effect and the cause are the female bee;
the eternal Self follows the male bee, and those two follow the female bee.
O Goddess, Bhramarī, the bearer of accomplishments, is the cause of them all;
she stands encompassing everything, [bestowing] the accomplishments of the lines of accomplishment.
O Supreme Goddess, the male bee is always directly the nature of Brahman;
O Goddess, the female bee is Unmanī, directly the very form of liberation.
O Goddess Padmāvatī, having stayed there, he indeed drinks the honey-wine,
beholding the eternal one who bestows liberation and is the very embodiment of liberation itself.
At that very moment, O my beloved, the essence of knowledge suddenly arose within me. The Lord said:
Listen now to another supreme knowledge, the most excellent lotus.
O Goddess, O my beloved, it is a marvel to me that you have been seen supported by the three qualities.
O Supreme Goddess, Rudra, Viṣṇu, and Pitāmaha are composed of the three guṇas;
yet all of them, O Supreme Goddess, exist in the form of women.
O Supreme Goddess, Vāmā is Brahmā himself with four faces;
endowed with the quality of rajas, Vāmā has a form and appearance like vermilion.
O Supreme Goddess, she who is Viṣṇu is always composed of the quality of sattva;
O Great Goddess, she is white in form and is eternally engaged in the act of protection.
O Great Goddess, she was seen with four arms, bearing the conch, discus, and mace, and praised by Sanaka and the others; hear now another marvel.
O Supreme Goddess, she who is Raudrī is Kṛṣṇā, O Supreme Sovereign;
having conquered me, O Supreme Goddess, she licks the three worlds.
Therefore, O Maheśānī, having shaken off my mental [conceptions],
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra always abide in female form.
O lady of pure smiles, Vāmā stands nearby holding the four Vedas, while Viṣṇu holds the fourteenth scripture.
O lady of pure smiles, O Maheśānī, having assumed the form of the Sūrya-śāstra and the Itihāsa, Rudra remains at the end of this [text], O beloved, with his feet joined to it.
O Maheśānī, Vāmā is said to be Brahmā, Jyeṣṭhā is Viṣṇu, and Raudrī should be known as Rudra; thus, O Supreme Goddess, she is the three qualities (triguṇa).
Indeed, a hundred million recitations of the Āgama were held in the hand of Sundarī;
she was chanting the Śrīvidyā, the sacred lore to be worshipped by me, which is the very embodiment of Brahman.
Having seen [this] in the city of Sadāśiva, wonder arises within me;
for you always abide in the city of Sadāśiva, assuming that supreme form.
That goddess is Sundarī, O Goddess, whose form enchants the world;
she is the primordial source of all things, from the immobile to the mobile, and is eternal.

Thereafter, O lady of excellent hips, having recited [the mantra] one hundred thousand times, O lady of pure smiles, and having first studied the Tantra— which is difficult even for the gods to obtain— O Great Goddess;
I shall proclaim; listen, O mature lady, to this secret Tantra, the highest of the high.

Of this venerable five-syllabled mantra (pañcākṣara-mantra), Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra are the seers (ṛṣis); the Ṛg, Yajus, Sāman, and Atharvan are the meters (chandāṃsi); and the venerable Mṛtyuñjaya is the deity for the sake of attaining the four aims of human life (caturvarga).
The application for the recitation (japa) is as follows:
O Maheśānī, having diligently performed the external recitation one hundred thousand times,
one should then offer it after carefully beholding a bilva leaf.
Having paid homage to the earthly linga which consists of the Supreme Brahman, O beloved,
and then having recited the armor-mantra (kavaca) for that linga, O lotus-faced one.
Now, the praise of the mouth-instrument (mukhavādya): O Supreme Goddess, having indeed made the mouth-instrument eternal,
the mouth-instrument accompanied by the Mātṛkā-mantra is very difficult to obtain.
O Supreme Goddess, having diligently uttered the letters from 'a' to 'kṣa' in both direct and reverse order, one should perform the oral musical instrument.
Having uttered each letter together with its bindu, O beloved, [one should recite] the fifty mātṛkās in direct and reverse order by means of sound, O fair-faced one.
Whoever plays a wind instrument according to this very method is a perfected one (siddha), he is Śiva, and he is also possessed of qualities (saguṇa); there is no doubt about this.
O Goddess of the gods, by the grace of this mouth-instrument, I am the conqueror of death;
O Maheśānī, at whatever time a demon might become powerful, [I shall overcome him].
At that time, O Maheśānī, I played a wind instrument;
hearing that, O Parameśānī, the Asuras who were stationed outside [were struck with fear].
O Maheśānī, O Parameśvarī, upon hearing that,
those who are new on this earth flee, O beloved, unless they possess a mouth-instrument.
Experiencing all those torments, he shall at the end become a *kumbhīra* (crocodile).
[Thus ends the eighth chapter in the Liṅgārcanatantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 8 ||
The Goddess said:
O Blessed One, Lord of the gods of gods, wielder of the trident, bearer of the Pināka bow;
O Moon among the lords of yoga, O mighty-armed one, O Conqueror of Death, salutations be unto you!
"O Lord of Gods, O you whose wealth is asceticism, when the dissolution has occurred and all things mobile and immobile have perished, from where were these sixteen modes of worship obtained?"
And at the time of breath control (prāṇāyāma), as well as during the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi),
O Lord, when the mind, intellect, and so forth dissolve there, O Mahādeva.
O Lord of Gods, in a mere moment, a hundred thousand years have passed for me;
the moon and sun have vanished from the sky—whence is night, and whence is day?
"O Supreme Lord, O Treasure of Austerities, from where does this number arise? The Lord said:
"O blessed lady, you have asked well; these words are like nectar."
O Great Goddess, your speech is always born of nectar.
O beloved, your speech is born of nectar and filled with laughter;
O beloved, my speech consists of the bliss of Brahman and is equal to yoga.
O Supreme Goddess, O Mistress of the Gods, O Radiant One, I meditate upon your body day and night through yoga, with manifold contemplations.
O Maheśānī, by great good fortune, I behold [thee] at the time of yoga;
O Maheśānī, I behold all of thy external knowledge.
Internal knowledge and external knowledge are your illusion, O fair-faced one;
your illusion is difficult to overcome when it is held in your hand.
O Goddess of gods, she who is the female bee and who wears the thread of the Siddhas—
O Goddess, everything, both the stationary and the moving, is established in you.
"O Queen of the Gods, O Beloved, I am the Conqueror of Death because of the touch of your limbs.
Listen, Pārvatī, I shall speak that which has been requested by you, my dear."
O Supreme Goddess, at the time of dissolution, when all things mobile and immobile have perished,
O Great Sovereign, everything— both that which is stationary and that which moves— is absorbed within me.
All those, O Goddess of gods, O beloved, remain eternally within my splendor, O fair-limbed one; everything, O passionate lady, remains within me.
But the fire-element, O Supreme Goddess, is always of the nature of Prakṛti;
I am devoid of qualities, O Great Goddess, eternally, O Supreme Sovereign.
O lady of pure smiles, you are indeed always possessed of attributes; yet you are also attribute-less.
Listen to a special teaching, which I shall declare—a secret that is most strictly to be guarded.
O Maheśānī, those who are the dwellers of the three heavens, beginning with Brahmā, and those who are mortals, O Parameśvarī, beginning with Kṣalā, [all worship] with devotion.
O Goddess with the lotus-face, there are others such as the Mātṛkās and men born of the Gandharva lineage, who dwell within the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa) as your devotees.
O Goddess, whatever [offerings] such as perfumes and flowers were given and offered by me unto me,
all that remains inexhaustible, O Supreme Sovereign.
O Queen of the Gods, O my beloved, O Mother, you remain eternally within the mass of my matted locks,
having performed worship with the sixteen services.
O Goddess, my central face is Īśāna, equal to Brahman;
O Maheśānī, whatever is offered there becomes entirely composed of Brahman.
Whatever is offered with a spirit of devotion through the sixteen modes of service,
all of it indeed becomes inexhaustible and remains within my matted locks.
O Supreme Goddess, O lady of pure smiles, whatever water is offered,
O Queen of the God of Gods, that water remains within my matted locks.
O Supreme Goddess, that Gaṅgā is supreme and pervades the entire universe;
O Goddess, she assumes a white form and is seated upon a white lotus throne.
Clad in white garments and adorned with white garlands,
she constantly wears earrings set with joined rubies.
The four-armed Mahāmāyā holds the gesture of fearlessness (abhaya) and the gesture of granting boons (varada);
O Goddess of gods, O Supreme Sovereign, she also holds a vessel of nectar (sudhākuṇḍa).
She who constantly desires to recite prayers wears a rosary of rudrākṣa beads;
indeed, the wearing of a prayer-bead rosary is the supreme means for performing japa.
O lady of beautiful limbs, hear that mantra of Kālikā which is very difficult to obtain;
O Maheśānī, O passionate one, listen as I shall speak the eight-syllabled mantra.
Having extracted the seed-syllable of desire (Kāma), then [the word] Kālike on the right;
having again extracted the desire-syllable, this is the eight-syllabled mantra, O Dear One.
Having become thus, that Gaṅgā remains forever upon the slope of my matted locks;
both the stationary and the moving worlds are situated within my mass of matted hair.
She who pervades the entire universe is celebrated as Gaṅgā;
that Gaṅgā, O Supreme Goddess, is the Sovereign Lady, eternal and imperishable.
That Goddess, in the form of water, always resides upon my head;
[I worship her] with these sixteen substances and with the various individual services (upacāras).
Having worshipped the earthen linga, O my beloved, there is external yoga;
without external yoga, O Goddess, internal yoga is not accomplished.
O Goddess, without internal yoga, external yoga does not succeed;
for this very reason, O Great Mistress, the worship of the *liṅga* has been performed by me.
O Goddess, without external worship, emanation does not arise;
O Great Mistress, without emanation, everything indeed falls into concealment.
Thus, O Maheśānī, is the truth regarding Gaṅgā’s origin from birth;
at the time of yoga, O Maheśānī, she has entered my millions of pores.
"All that is seen exists within the radiant energy (tejas), and all is established within primordial nature (prakṛti).
If you do not know this knowledge, O passionate woman, then listen to it.
Then, O Goddess of gods, O fair-faced one, what shall I do by means of yoga? O Great Goddess, all this is always situated upon the path of yoga.
O lady of noble hips, the path of yoga is joined with the fifty principles;
for the supreme principle is knowledge, the imperishable form of primordial nature.
O beloved Pārvatī, Prakṛti is the form of Brahmā, which deludes the three worlds;
everything from Lomaya onwards up to the Varṣa region remains within it.
Having seen this, O Maheśānī, I perform it a hundred thousand times;
for the Gaṅgā is indeed the causal water that always resides within the mass of matted hair.
O Maheśānī of pure smiles, the source of the Gaṅgā’s origin is supreme; it is my matted locks, O Goddess.
O Supreme Goddess, when the dissolution has occurred and all things mobile and immobile have perished,
at that time, O Great Goddess, the Primordial Cause swiftly arrived.
O Goddess of gods, O Pārvatī, that Gaṅgā quickly spoke these words to me in my presence with a subtle voice, as before.
O Lord, best among ascetics, Supreme Soul, salutations be unto you!
O Gaurī’s Lord, Mahādeva, O Master, be gracious toward me.
O God, when the moon and sun were invisible in the sky, O wielder of the trident;
when all things moving and unmoving, O Supreme Lord, had become invisible.
What shall I do? Where shall I go? Speak the truth, O ocean of compassion!
O Goddess, O mighty-armed one, O Conqueror of Death, salutations be unto you! Please grant me a place of refuge.
Īśvara said:
Having heard her words regarding that cause, listen to what I shall say:
"Come, O fawn-eyed one, O supreme goddess, for the sake of this matter."
O Maheśānī, you who abide within the mass of matted locks, salutations to you!
O highly fortunate one, you are Prakṛti, the destroyer of all sins.
Save me, O lady of tremulous glances, auspicious one who bears a white form!
O Great Goddess, your matted locks are the unsurpassed abode of the Gaṅgā.
There, the Gaṅgā is eternally pervaded by Prakṛti, the Supreme Goddess;
and whatever [form] I possess, O Queen of Gods, that is directly the form of Prakṛti.

O fair-faced one, with its waters it has the luster of the color of tawny gold and resembles a thousand suns; it is a divine mass of matted hair consisting of pure light, which is liberation itself in visible form.
O Goddess, when she was within his matted locks, she who removes all sins was called Mahāgaṅgā by the Vedas, O Supreme Sovereign.
That divine Mahāgaṅgā resides upon the slope of the matted locks;
she is the wave of bliss, eternally dissolved in bliss.
That Gaṅgā, O Great Goddess, who is herself the embodiment of Śakti,
always resides within the mass of matted hair accompanied by bilva leaves.
O Goddess, having conquered death, I now abide for your sake;
just as Gaṅgā is dear to you, O Goddess, so too shall I possess freedom from old age and death.
O Goddess, through the power of the Great Gaṅgā, one attains freedom from old age and death;
for that Great Gaṅgā bestows the eight sovereign powers.
Therefore, O lady of beautiful limbs, beloved of Mahādeva, remain forever within your matted locks, which are like the pure water of the causal ocean that removes all sins.
From that point onward, however, the Gaṅgā became stationary upon the slope of his matted locks;
seeing her beautiful on the slope of the matted hair, adorned with various flowers.
O beautiful one, O amorous woman, whatever was seen upon my matted locks— endowed with various perfumes and adorned with various jewels.
But as soon as Kāraṇī Gaṅgā was seen, she herself departed;
that which was witnessed within the matted locks of hair is simply impossible to describe.
O Goddess of gods, that Gaṅgā who resides in the matted locks [of Śiva], renowned as Ādigaṅgā, is the eternal Śvetagaṅgā, the very life-force of all beings.
Īśvara said:
O Maheśānī, the pair of Gaṅgās always resides upon my head;
whatever is seen, whether gross or subtle, O Parameśvarī.
O Goddess, O lady of pure smiles, everything belongs to me within the mass of matted locks;
yet, O Supreme Goddess, those matted locks are white in form and captivating.
O Great Goddess, O lady of excellent complexion, my matted locks have eight forms, resembling camphor and possessing a luster equal to white clouds.
O lady of beautiful hips, she always resides upon the matted locks on his eight limbs; O beloved, having worshipped the earthen linga with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings, [she dwells there].
O beloved, all those preliminary services are the very nature [of the practice];
thereafter, O Great Goddess, follows the flower and sandalwood paste which bestow happiness.
O Goddess, various kinds of food offerings— both fragrant and devoid of scent—
as well as bilva leaves, white water lilies, tagara, and jasmine;
O Goddess, [offer] mālatī, yūthikā, and the enchanting karavīra;
O Beloved, likewise the lotus, ketakī, kunda, and āmalakī.
Having offered the kumuda, the kokanada, and beautiful flowers of the four colors, as well as dūrvā grass and tulasī, one should worship the earthen image.
O Pārvatī, as for other flowers such as the *dhustūra* and others,
through my knowledge, a flower is seen that is identical to the *dhustūra*.
O Parameśānī, the Dhustūra flower is the very embodiment of liberation;
O Deveśī, O Parameśvarī, it yields that same fruit which is obtained from the gift of ten million cows.
O Pārvatī, whatever flowers there may be that fill the entire universe, they attain equality with the offering of the *dhustūra* flower.
Having set aside all those various incenses and diverse lamps upon the earthen vessel, O Goddess of the Gods.
O beloved, perform the other services according to the prescribed method.
[Thus ends the ninth chapter in the Śrīliṅgārcanatantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 9 ||
Īśvara said:
"O Goddess, having worshipped the earthen Śiva according to the prescribed rite, I have achieved my purpose, O Maheśānī; everything, O lady of pure smiles, rests upon you."
O Maheśānī, at the time of worship, my [time] has passed for a long duration;
thus, having placed a leaf of Vijayā upon the earthen vessel.
Having offered a leaf of *vijayā*, one obtains the fruit of an *aśvamedha* sacrifice;
indeed, by properly performing oral music, one has reached my presence ten million times over.
O Goddess of gods, O fair-faced one, having seen my *tāṇḍava* dance and the playing of musical instruments from my mouth, O Supreme Goddess, O beloved, the *liṅga* was then split asunder.
Then, O blessed one, Prakṛti herself appeared before you, O passionate lady;
Mahāmāyā manifested for the protection of the worlds.
O Maheśānī, having seen the Goddess who is the very embodiment of liberation,
Mahāmāyā stood by her side accompanied by ten musical instruments.
"O Parameśānī of excellent vows, you have attained perfection through your worship;
having heard her words, [he] fell at her feet."
O Goddess of gods, whatever water for the feet, the respectful offering (arghya), and so forth is given with a spirit of devotion;
O Supreme Sovereign, whatever is offered remains situated upon the head of the Gaṅgā.
O Supreme Goddess, that Gaṅgā is established within her lotus;
having become the mother of the three worlds, she is likewise situated throughout the three worlds.
O Parameśānī, O lady of pure smiles, listen to that which was given to that Goddess; O Maheśānī, O sinless one, I shall speak it to you.
Īśvara said:
Obeisance be to you, O Supreme Goddess, whose glory is supreme bliss;
you who are the manifest bestower of dharma, truth, desire, and wealth at all times.
Salutations to you, O Mother of the worlds; salutations to you, O destroyer of sins. O Supreme Goddess, worshipped with jewels, when the universe has perished, [salutations to you].
"What shall I do? I am going away, my mind agitated by anxiety, O beautiful one, after having worshipped the earthen linga with many vehicles."
This very day, my worship has become fruitful through the sight of your glorious feet;
I have attained my life's purpose, O Great Goddess, by beholding your glorious feet.
O Maheśānī, whatever captivating offering has been given,
O Parameśānī, I behold all of that at your feet.
Grant a boon, O Mahāmāyā, you who cause the creation and destruction of the universe!
O Goddess, the entire world that previously existed, both the stationary and the moving.
"O Goddess, by that very method, cause the universe to fall;
beyond this, O beloved, Mahāmāyā shall hear my auspicious word."
Taking a liṅga fashioned from sandalwood and placed upon her left finger,
she created the supreme and beautiful Pūtanī, who is identical with the universe.
Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, Raudrī, and Pūtanī—this is what is traditionally taught.
O Maheśānī, Vāmā is said to be Brahmā, while Jyeṣṭhā is celebrated as Viṣṇu.
Then, O Pārvatī, having emanated Raudrī by means of the *prāṇa*-mantra,
and having performed the consecration of the vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*) there, O Queen of Gods, O lady of pure smiles;
At the time of the installation of the vital breath (prāṇapratiṣṭhā), O Yogavardhinī, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra were seen, along with the qualities of rajas, sattva, and tamas.
O Supreme Sovereign, O Beloved, at that very moment those gods appeared before Pūtanā, O Great Goddess; this is the truth, the absolute truth, O lady of pure smiles.
Having manifested three forms, he vanished right there;
when he had disappeared, O fair-faced one, I became composed of pure consciousness.
